saints.name: St. Lidwina of Schiedam
saints.title: Virgin
saints.shortBlurb: A Dutch maiden whose thirty-eight years of illness became a school of redemptive suffering…
biography: Born at Schiedam in Holland on 18 April 1380, one of a laborer's nine children, Lidwina fell while skating at fifteen and broke a rib. The injury never healed; sickness crept over her limb by limb until she lay bedridden — by her biographers' account paralyzed but for one hand — for the last thirty-eight years of her life.

She offered her sufferings for sinners and lived in union with the Passion; her fasts grew so extreme that the magistrates of Schiedam drew up a document, which survives, attesting that she took almost no nourishment. Cures and multiplied alms were credited to her prayers, and the sick of Holland came to her bedside as to a shrine.

She died on 14 April 1433, aged fifty-two, and her grave became a place of pilgrimage; the friar John Brugman wrote her life, and Thomas à Kempis spread her fame. Leo XIII granted her equipollent canonization on 14 March 1890. Because her passion began on the ice she is patroness of skaters; because she bore it thirty-eight years, of the chronically ill.
saints.knownFor: Bearing long illness as an offering of redemptive suffering.

canonization.canonized: Cult confirmed 1890 by Pope Leo XIII

sources.text: Butler, Lives of the Saints (1866 ed.), 14 April
